content: Linguist detection is an ordered strategy cascade (from source lib/linguist.rb): STRATEGIES = [Modeline, Filename, Shebang, Extension, XML, Manpage, Heuristics, Classifier]. Each strategy receives candidate languages from the previous one and narrows them; the first strategy that yields exactly one candidate wins; returns nil if no strategy resolves (unknown language is a nil/empty result, NOT an error). Heuristics inspect only the first 50KB of content. Snyk's detector (parallel ecosystem finding): ordered DETECTABLE_FILES basename list (go.mod, package.json, pom.xml, build.gradle(.kts), composer.lock...) — first existing file wins, mapped to package manager by basename table. mise/asdf walk up the tree for .nvmrc, .python-version, rust-toolchain.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml and extract only the runtime version. Pattern takeaways for best-effort project detection: (1) ordered first-match manifest cascade is simple/deterministic/low-maintenance; (2) unknown = typed fallback value, never error; (3) skip vendored/generated dirs (linguist vendor.yml hygiene).
